描述_ZN: The Water Walk at the End of the Forest" scroll, Ming dynasty, painted by Dong Qichang, on paper with ink brush, 115.8 cm in length and 45.3 cm in width.　　The picture shows a sparse forest, a gentle river, deep valleys and deep mountains. The title reads, "The limits of the forest are indistinguishable, and the steps of the water are difficult to distinguish. Painted by Xuanzai", with the inscriptions "Bachelor of Zongbo" and "Dong's Xuanzai" in white. Inscriptions: "Xiyi" in white characters, "Xuzhai Review" in white characters, "Pang Leshen Collection Seal" in vermilion characters, "Sun Yufeng Collection Seal" in vermilion characters. Seal" in vermilion and "Sun Yufeng Collection Seal" in vermilion. On the right side of the frame, "Susanna Susanna Seal" in white and "Temporarily obtained in their own pleasure" in vermilion.　　The line "The limit of the forest is indistinguishable, and the water step is hard to distinguish" is from the five-word poem "Looking at the Faraway Village" by Monk Kyauk Ryeo, the tenth grandson of Xie Lingyun of the Southern Dynasty during the period from Dali to Zhenyuan of the Tang Dynasty, and the full poem reads as follows: "The limit of the forest is indistinguishable, and the water step is hard to distinguish. The village can be seen vaguely by the verdant edge of a mountain." (See Quan Tang Poems, vol. 820). Pang Laichen's "Xuzhai Famous Paintings Continued" Volume II recorded this picture as "Dong Wenmin's Forests and Mountains" axis.　　Dong Qichang's landscape halo more than chapped, to get the show Run Hua zhi state. The layout is not too cumbersome, simple and crisp, and the mood is clear and elegant, which makes people feel relaxed and happy.
